summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia in remission following double cord blood transplant, was admitted for evaluation of a painful right lower extremity rash concerning for cellulitis. He presented with erythema, warmth, and inability to bear weight, but no trauma or fever. Initial treatment included IV vancomycin and cefepime. Imaging showed no evidence of osteomyelitis or DVT, and blood cultures remained negative. The rash improved significantly, and he was transitioned to oral clindamycin and ciprofloxacin for completion at home. Acute kidney injury was noted, likely due to medication or dehydration, and managed with temporary discontinuation of lisinopril. His vision concerns were evaluated and attributed to chronic steroid use, with ophthalmology follow-up arranged. He remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, monitor for recurrence, and follow up with specialists.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
